extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans of comedy, and researchers seeking biographical information on Greg Giraldo
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia biography of stand-up comedian Greg Giraldo covering his background, education, career, comedic style, notable appearances, and personal life. Useful for understanding his work, themes, and career milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Observational comedy; black comedy; surreal humor; insult comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in the article's infobox as the primary comedic styles associated with Greg Giraldo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Current events; everyday life; self-deprecation; marriage; parenting; pop culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under the infobox 'Subjects'; the article also notes he incorporated personal struggles (addiction, life on the road) into his material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infobox designation; the article details his work across live stand-up venues and numerous television programs, specials, and panels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notable work / appearances
rubrics_metrics.description: Tough Crowd with Colin Quinn; Stand-Up Nation; Comedy Central Roasts; Lewis Black's Root of All Evil; The Greg Giraldo Show; Comedy Central specials; Late Night/Letterman/Kimmel appearances; hosting The Nasty Show; Bonnaroo performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article enumerates specific shows, roast appearances, TV roles, and specials as markers of his career and prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance formats and venues
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy clubs (e.g., Comedy Cellar); festivals (Just for Laughs, Bonnaroo); USO tour (Guantanamo Bay); late-night television; television specials; albums; tours (Indecision '08).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and dates are given (USO tour 2002, Just for Laughs appearances, Comedy Central Presents specials, Midlife Vices one-hour special, album releases) illustrating the range of formats in which he performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Roast and insult-comedy specialty
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequently appeared on Comedy Central's televised roast specials and was known for insult comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article lists numerous roast appearances (Chevy Chase, Pamela Anderson, William Shatner, Jeff Foxworthy, Flavor Flav, Bob Saget, Joan Rivers, Larry the Cable Guy, David Hasselhoff, etc.) and identifies 'insult comedy' in the genre field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career milestones / achievements
rubrics_metrics.description: Hosted Stand-Up Nation; multiple Comedy Central specials (two half-hour, one one-hour Midlife Vices); album releases (Good Day to Cross a River, Midlife Vices); headlined tours and served as a judge on Last Comic Standing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article provides dates and context for specials, albums, tours and television roles that mark career progression and recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal background and education
rubrics_metrics.description: Born in Queens to Colombian and Spanish parents; BA in English from Columbia University; J.D. from Harvard Law School; briefly practiced corporate law (Skadden, Arps) before turning to comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education and early legal career are documented and presented as part of his biography and public narrative; the article includes anecdotes (e.g., pro bono defense of Jeffrey Ross) showing how background intersected with his comedy career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Themes in material: addiction and recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Giraldo was candid about struggles with drug and alcohol addiction and often incorporated these themes into his act; he later stated he had freed himself from addiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article details rehab history, sobriety markers (tattoo '525'), and how addiction/recovery informed both material and posthumous tributes/benefit events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influences and comedic approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Claimed he was 'influenced by the (crappy) people' and learned by watching poor performers; self-deprecating and candid approach informed his style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted remarks explain his formative influences and approach to comedy, providing insight into his development of tone and delivery (e.g., embracing insult and candid personal material).
